closure_basis.subject: Output-only request
closure_basis.assessment: The actual shared dialogue mb_hostentity.h sends exactly the segment and candidate pose (18 stationary or 22 moving floats). It neither loads, copies nor forwards the caller point/normal. Existing real callers remain unchanged, including the output-only normal locals in weapon and hosted LOS paths. This removes the indeterminate-storage read instead of concealing it by initializing callers.

closure_basis.subject: Computed writes only
closure_basis.assessment: The kernel starts with its own initialized output vectors and records the normal assignment before each intersection helper, and the point assignment immediately after each whole-point assignment. The mask accumulates over the existing ordered face/sweep walk, retaining a previously written point even when a later face only replaces the normal. Unassigned components are zero in the answer and are not committed by Core. The two point-assignment markers are the only intersection-text differences from the closed tree copy; arithmetic and sweep/face order are not changed by this correction.

closure_basis.subject: Complete validation before commit
closure_basis.assessment: The actual adapter requires the correct scene and hit/miss discriminator; accepts only six-bit, whole-vector masks; rejects point-without-normal and a hit without both vectors; and rejects any nonzero raw word for an unassigned component, including negative zero. All checks finish before either caller buffer is touched. Computed assigned words are copied as bytes, normal first then point; unassigned caller words remain unread and byte-exact, including signaling-NaN payloads.

closure_basis.subject: Transport and ABI
closure_basis.assessment: C and Rust append write_mask at the same reply position. Request counts are consistently changed to 18/22 across C, Engine and the host provider. Lua validates an integral mask within 0..63; Engine carries it with checked C-int conversion. C remains the authority for full mask relationships before buffer commit. Six computed output words preserve the existing exact-bit string transport, including nonfinite bit patterns; other model finite-only parsing remains unchanged.

closure_basis.subject: Kernel lifetime and error paths
closure_basis.assessment: The existing synchronous model cursor, guarded host arithmetic, refusal conversion and final announced-order ModelStore are reused. The per-thread assignment record resets for each kernel entry, is accumulated only by that invocation on the production store cursor path, and is cleared from refused results. No caller output is read by kernel initialization or return. No new callback lifetime or original solver fallback is introduced.

closure_basis.subject: Build boundary and original behavior
closure_basis.assessment: The unchanged ordinary/original profile selection remains as reviewed at c510. The isolated dialogue C test is behind entity-dialogue-check and includes the exact production header. It is a boundary test with a scripted host, not a retail or model-numeric oracle. Original callers and collision characterization bodies are not initialized or rewritten.
